Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with 3–4 months of painful, itchy, cracked skin on the palms, worsening recently and impairing work; clinical impression of contact dermatitis likely related to occupational exposure to cleaning agents with inconsistent glove use; topical steroid and emollients prescribed; advised trigger avoidance and close follow-up in 10–14 days.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful, cracked, dry skin on hands (palms), with intermittent itch.
- Onset/duration: Began ~3–4 months ago.
- Course/progression: Gradual worsening; now significantly painful and interfering with work; required 3 days off work.
- Location: Primarily palms; general mild dryness on legs (longstanding, not severe).
- Associated symptoms:
  - Itch present intermittently.
  - Bleeding only after scratching; no spontaneous bleeding.
  - Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms.
  - Appetite, eating, and drinking adequate.
- Exacerbating/initiating factors: Occupational exposure to cleaning products; inconsistent glove use; job change to hotel housekeeping ~4 months ago.
- Relieving measures tried:
  - Emollient (E45) with no benefit.
  - Antihistamine with no benefit (name/dose not documented).
- Systems review (pertinent negatives): No systemic symptoms as above; no prior diagnosed eczema/dermatitis.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus. No reported complications mentioned.
  - Medication associated: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No known prior skin conditions (eczema/dermatitis denied).
- No asthma or bowel disease history.

Social History:
- Occupation: Hotel housekeeper; cleans bedrooms/bathrooms; regular exposure to cleaning agents; inconsistent glove use.
- Work impact: Unable to work for the past 3 days due to hand pain.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks a couple of pints per week (minimal).
- Lifestyle: Patient reports generally not hydrating much.

Family History:
- Diabetes in family.
- No known family history of skin conditions, asthma, or bowel disorders.

Physical Examination:


Investigations:
- None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected irritant/contact dermatitis of the hands (palmar), occupational exposure to cleaning chemicals; worsened over 3–4 months; intermittent itch; fissuring and pain; bleeding only with scratching; no systemic symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Avoid triggers; wear protective gloves consistently during cleaning.
    - Start topical steroid cream for palmar dermatitis (name/potency/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript).
    - Start stronger emollients; apply generously 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
    - Prescription to be sent to patient’s pharmacy.
    - Follow-up in 10–14 days to assess response; return sooner if worsening, spreading, or no improvement.
    - Consider alternative or additional treatments if no improvement at follow-up.

- General plan items:
  - Education on skin care: minimize exposure to irritants, frequent moisturizing, avoid scratching.
  - Work guidance: use gloves at all times when handling cleaning agents.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vital signs and physical examination findings.
  - Specific topical steroid name, potency, dosing instructions.
  - Specific emollient product name.
  - Full medication list reconciliation beyond metformin.
  - Diabetes control details (A1c, complications), vaccinations, and screening history not discussed.
  - Allergy status documented as none; no details on environmental/contact allergies.
● Internal conflicts:
  - Bleeding denied initially but later clarified to occur only after scratching (no spontaneous bleeding).
● Transcript quality:
  - Some inaudible/unclear segments; key clinical details largely intact.
